trust_decision.summary: Which peer may supply the client IP (X-Forwarded-For/X-Real-IP) is decided once, engine-wide, by gin SetTrustedProxies in InitRouter; at the pinned commit nothing is trusted, so behind the bundled Docker nginx every request has ClientIP 127.0.0.1, which the IP allowlist exempts and the login ban keys on as one shared bucket.

landing_point.why: The summary names IP allowlists and the loopback exemption is visible here; the lockout half leads to api/user/auth.go:51. The real cause is the engine trusted-proxy setting in another package (router/routers.go:47).

fix_sites.entry_point: every HTTP route on the cosy/gin engine (engine-level SetTrustedProxies; fix.diff:1824-1827)
same engine-wide; new router/client_ip.go picks trusted proxies by topology via helper.ShouldManageBundledNginx (internal/helper/docker.go:21-24)
app.ini [auth] / env NGINX_UI_AUTH_TRUSTED_PROXIES; POST /api/settings binding (fix.diff:1839 adds TrustedProxies with ip|cidr|redacted, protected)

/api/* group (router/routers.go:64), /mcp and /mcp_message (mcp/router.go:39, mcp/router.go:43), embedded static (router/routers_embed.go:16); fix drops the empty-ClientIP fail-open (fix.diff:1409-1410)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: router/routers.go:47 (engine default SetTrustedProxies(nil); the fix replaces it with a topology-aware default merged with the configured TrustedProxies, fix.diff:1663-1682)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The router bootstrap looks like generic framework setup, and `SetTrustedProxies(nil)` reads as already hardened. A solver could argue the bug is the loopback exemption in the middleware and leave the proxy topology alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Direct loopback clients must still pass the allowlist. X-Forwarded-For/X-Real-IP from untrusted peers must still be ignored. Deployments without the bundled nginx (NGINX_UI_DISABLE_BUNDLED_NGINX, non-Docker) must not start trusting loopback. Trusting all proxies, or removing the loopback exemption, breaks one of these.

O6_input_shapes: single X-Forwarded-For value via the bundled loopback proxy
IPv6 loopback peer ::1 with an IPv6 forwarded client
multi-hop X-Forwarded-For chain, stopping at the first untrusted hop
spoofed X-Forwarded-For from an untrusted direct peer
invalid/unparseable RemoteAddr giving an empty ClientIP (now fails closed)
TrustedProxies entries as IP or CIDR, plus the redacted placeholder on settings save

O7_producer.where: settings/auth.go:3-12 (AuthSettings, loaded from app.ini/env; the fix adds TrustedProxies) consumed once at router/routers.go:47 at startup

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The node-auth failure log could read X-Real-IP / X-Forwarded-For directly instead of ClientIP().
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Diagnostic logging that wants the 'real' client behind a proxy often reads the header directly, bypassing the engine trust list.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Passkey login ban-clear (or an OTP/2FA attempt limiter) keyed on c.Request.RemoteAddr or a raw header.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A second auth entry point written separately from Login could pick a different client-IP source; it would still be shared 127.0.0.1 behind the bundled proxy.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The MCP route could use its own allowlist helper that trusts X-Forwarded-For from any peer.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: MCP is registered on the engine outside the /api group with its own middleware chain, so a separate implementation there is plausible.
